title: Long-tail Usage Telemetry Sentinel: reduce noisy alerts on low-exposure customers
creator: Marissa Chen
description: Problem: The console telemetry pipeline produces an outsized number of alerts coming from low-exposure (long-tail) customers and transient sampling artifacts. These noisy alerts reduce SRE/PM trust in the system and delay response to genuine platform regressions. Goal: Build a "Long-tail Telemetry Sentinel" that reduces false positives by combining exposure-aware scoring, adaptive thresholds, and lightweight context enrichment (customer cohorts, recent deploys, region, plan). The sentinel will live as a post-ingest enrichment stage in the usage analytics pipeline and produce an "anomaly_score" + signal metadata for downstream alerting and runbook generation. Key design choices: 1) Use exposure-normalized z-scores to avoid flagging small customers for percentage-level variance. 2) Augment with a fast change-point detector (CUSUM) to catch abrupt platform-level regressions. 3) Add a feedback path where alert acknowledgements (incidents) are used to tune thresholds for customer cohorts. 4) Provide a sane default attenuation policy: for customers with 95th percentile daily tokens < threshold, scale down alert priority and suppress ephemeral spikes. Work scope: - implement enrichment job in backend pipeline (Spark/beam-compatible) - add redis-backed short-term cache for recent deploy markers and experiment flags - extend alert router to accept anomaly_score and signal_metadata - update console alert UI to surface exposure and evidence links - document runbook and escalation rules Success metrics: 40% reduction in alerts classified as "no-action" in first 30 days, median time-to-detect true-platform-regression unaffected (<5m), <5% missed regressions in retrospective sampling
tasks: Design enrichment proto and anomaly_score schema
Implement exposure-normalized scoring module in pipeline worker
Add deploy marker ingestion and cache layer
Integrate CUSUM change-point detector as optional heuristics module
Add alert router changes to respect attenuation and re-prioritization
Console UI: show exposure, evidence links, and suggested next steps
Write runbook and postmortem template updates
E2E tests + simulation harness with synthetic long-tail traffic
Canary rollout to non-prod orgs then controlled prod rollout
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline outputs anomaly_score and signal_metadata for each alerting candidate
Alerts for low-exposure customers are attenuated according to policy by default
Dashboard shows a 40% reduction in "no-action" alerts in week-1 sampling
Ability to toggle CUSUM heuristics per-namespace via feature flag
Runbook page linked from every alert and contains direct reproduction links and suggested escalation
Post-deploy simulation: >=95% detection rate for injected platform regressions
